title.sl: Odvisni govor: she said she was tired
title.de: Indirekte Rede: she said she was tired
title.it: Il discorso indiretto: she said she was tired
title.en: What was said: she said she was tired

rule.sl:
**say** + kaj: **She said she was tired.** (Rekla je, da je utrujena.) **tell** + komu: **She told me she was tired.** Tudi **said to me**, ne *said me*. **told me**, ne *told to me*. **that** lahko izpustiš.

Čas gre korak nazaj: **am, is → was**, **are → were**, **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. Preteklik: **I saw Jack → He said he had seen Jack**, tudi **he saw Jack**. Slovenščina ostane v sedanjiku, angleščina ne.

Če je še vedno res, ljudje čas pustijo: **She said she's tired.** Tudi to je prav.

Zamenjaj osebo in besede za kraj in čas: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**, **now → then**.

Ukaz: **told me to** + osnovna oblika: **She told me to wait.** **told me not to**: **She told me not to wait.** Prošnja: **She asked me to wait.**
rule.de:
**say** + was: **She said she was tired.** (Sie sagte, sie sei müde.) **tell** + wem: **She told me she was tired.** Auch **said to me**, nicht *said me*. **told me**, nicht *told to me*. **that** kannst du weglassen.

Die Zeit geht einen Schritt zurück: **am, is → was**, **are → were**, **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. Die Vergangenheit: **I saw Jack → He said he had seen Jack**, auch **he saw Jack**. Englisch kennt keinen Konjunktiv dafür.

Wenn es noch stimmt, lassen die Leute die Zeit: **She said she's tired.** Auch das ist richtig.

Wechsle die Person und die Wörter für Ort und Zeit: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**, **now → then**.

Befehl: **told me to** + Grundform: **She told me to wait.** **told me not to**: **She told me not to wait.** Bitte: **She asked me to wait.**
rule.it:
**say** + che cosa: **She said she was tired.** (Ha detto che era stanca.) **tell** + a chi: **She told me she was tired.** Anche **said to me**, non *said me*. **told me**, non *told to me*. **that** si può togliere.

Il tempo fa un passo indietro: **am, is → was**, **are → were**, **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. Il passato: **I saw Jack → He said he had seen Jack**, anche **he saw Jack**.

Se è ancora vero, spesso il tempo resta: **She said she's tired.** Anche questo è giusto.

Cambia la persona e le parole di luogo e tempo: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**, **now → then**.

Un ordine: **told me to** + la forma base: **She told me to wait.** **told me not to**: **She told me not to wait.** Una richiesta: **She asked me to wait.**
rule.en:
**say** + what: **She said she was tired.** **tell** + who: **She told me she was tired.** Also **said to me**, not *said me*. **told me**, not *told to me*. You can leave out **that**.

The tense goes one step back: **am, is → was**, **are → were**, **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. The past: **I saw Jack → He said he had seen Jack**, also **he saw Jack**.

If it's still so, people keep the tense: **She said she's tired.** That's right too.

Change the person and the words for place and time: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**, **now → then**.

An order: **told me to** + the base form: **She told me to wait.** **told me not to**: **She told me not to wait.** A request: **She asked me to wait.**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina reče *Rekla je, da je utrujena*, angleščina **she was tired**, korak nazaj.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch hat dafür den Konjunktiv (*sie sei müde*), Englisch geht einen Schritt zurück: **she was tired**.
tip.it: 💡 Anche l'italiano fa un passo indietro (*era stanca*); ricorda **tell** + a chi: **She told me**.
tip.en: 💡 **tell** always says who: **She told me**; **say** doesn't: **She said**.
